statement: A failed-join withdrawal no longer relies on a pure in-memory reconcile queue that teardown destroys: either a withdrawal intent is persisted before teardown so a later run completes it, or lease-expiry is explicitly documented as the designed fallback (the choice recorded in a finding), and a status-column and endpoint-row reaper alongside the existing lease sweep removes the residual stale rows that today no writer ever drives to STOPPED. doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/durable-withdrawal-cleanup-intent-v2.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — withdrawal-intent-durability and stale-row-reaper receipts passing (deterministic red-on-revert evidence harness).

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Choose one and record it in a finding: persist a withdrawal intent before teardown (durable retry owner), OR explicitly document lease-expiry as the designed fallback. Do not leave DEFERRED silently meaning 'not applied' with no owner.

Any reaper must drive the status column to STOPPED and reap endpoint rows, complementing (not replacing) the leader's lease sweep and the active-node projection's stale-lease trim; leftovers must be stale rows, not live routing targets.
Each new regression test must fail when the durable-intent or reaper mechanism is reverted while the rest of the change remains.
